Fed: a December 9 hike was fully priced after Tuesday's CPI (50 bp odds 15%); the report's calendar has Hammack, Williams and Daly speaking Thursday.
Oil: Brent 93.97 (+1.3%), WTI 87.29 (+0.9%) at 8:13 after dipping earlier. Trump says no Iran deal is needed; Bernstein sees de-escalation as more likely and cut COP, FANG and DVN to market-perform.
China and chips: Sen. Cotton urges Commerce to ban Chinese memory maker CXMT. Asia fell (Hang Seng −1.4%, Kospi −0.6%); Europe's tech index −1.3%, ASML −3%.

bigPicture: The AI trade's question this morning is who runs Nvidia. The board met Wednesday after the NYT reported a second relationship, this time with a direct report; Oppenheimer and Bernstein downgraded, and earnings are Nov 17. Chips sell together; AMD and Broadcom are the only gainers.

Nebius shows the funding worry from the cost side: revenue grew 571% and beat, but capex is rising much faster than revenue guidance ($27B this year, $40–45B in 2027) and it raised $5.75B of debt. The leveraged AI cloud names give back yesterday's CoreWeave rally.
Rates are still a headwind: a December hike is fully priced, the 2-year rose 5 bp and the 10-year sits at 5.01%. Money is moving to energy, health care and staples.
Yesterday's +4.8% SMH bounce is being tested at once: SMH is +0.5% over 5 days and −10.2% over a month.
snapshot.takeaway: Today is headline-driven: an Nvidia board decision could land at any time in the session and move the whole chip group either way, so level setups in chips can be overridden in a minute. Let the first 15 minutes set the range (yesterday's real move started after 9:45), and remember Applied Materials, Cisco and Cerebras report after the close.

sectors.text: Nvidia −8.3% on the CEO reports and two downgrades; MU −5.3%, TSM −3.5%, INTC −4.0% (Xeon delays), AMAT −2.8% before tonight's report. AMD (+0.8%, William Blair upgrade) and AVGO (+0.4%) are the exceptions as possible share gainers. Sen. Cotton's call to ban China's CXMT is a small plus for MU.

Nebius beat on revenue but guided 2026 revenue to the low end and lifted capex to $27B this year and $40–45B in 2027, after raising $5.75B of debt. CRWV −10.5% and ORCL −3.6% give back part of yesterday's rally.

Nebius's bigger capex plan is more spending on power and cooling on paper, but VRT is −4.0% with the AI cloud names, below yesterday's 202.01 low. The report's data-center-limits risk still hangs over the group.

IGV −1.5% premarket after +1.9% yesterday; PLTR −1.8%, MSFT −0.7%, GOOGL −1.0% after an EU court adviser backed a $1.7B Google fine. Rising short-term yields keep high-multiple software on the losing side in the report.

XLE +1.1% premarket and XOM +1.2% as money hides in energy; Brent 93.97 (+1.3%) and WTI 87.29 (+0.9%) turned up after slipping earlier. Trump says no Iran deal is needed; Bernstein downgraded COP, FANG and DVN, seeing de-escalation as more likely, a risk for the E&Ps.
